newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond issuance may shift into high gear.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond issuance may shift into high gear.

text.p: The latest U.S. Treasury rally is expected to lure corporations back into the primary debt arena shifting issuance into high gear, dealers said.
"We should see a lot of activity next week with Treasury yields at these levels," said one syndicate source.

Issuers recently kept at bay by higher Treasury yields, and fears of a potential Federal Reserve hike in interest rates, are expected to take full advantage of the favorable rate environment and meet their financing needs now, dealers added.
"There's still no official calendar; however, rates at these levels will definitely spur issuers to come back to market," another syndicate source said.
News of a weaker-than-expected consumer inflation report sent the U.S. 30-year T-bond sharply higher, causing Treasury yields to back up substantially, dealers said.
Earlier, the U.S. Labor Department reported a slight 0.1 percent increase in the August consumer price index and the core rate.
In a Reuter poll, U.S. economists had predicted an increase of 0.2 percent in consumer prices and the core.

Recent subdued inflation reports on both the wholesale and consumer levels have helped to ease fears of an impending rate hike at the next meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee on September 24, dealers added.
Meanwhile, dealers said issuers have been given a window of opportunity in which to finance their debt at less costly levels.
As of midmorning Friday, dealers were looking for the pace to pick up substantially next week.
On Thursday, the following issuers tapped the market, dealers said.
Anixter Inc priced $100 million in seven-year notes to yield 135 basis points over Treasuries via Merrill Lynch.
Comerica priced $150 million in 30-year debt to yield 85 basis points over Treasuries via CS First Boston.
Associates Corp of North America priced $400 million in three-year notes to yield 26 basis points over Treasuries via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Lastly, Pearson Inc priced $250 million in 10-year medium-term notes rated A1/A-plus at a 63 basis point spread via Merrill.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was trading up 44/32 at 97-11/32 to yield 6.96 percent compared with Thursday's close at 7.07 percent.
